This is me in my Danang city, a beautiful and peaceful city with mountains and beaches. ::: {.column width="60%"}
Like I said, I started studying abroad in 10th grade. I went to a boarding school in a small town called Bettendorf in Iowa. That was the first time I actually learned science subjects in an interactive and hands-on setting with laboratory rather than just memorizing facts and rules. I soon found my love for doing science, specifically biology and biochemistry. Coming into college, I wanted to pursue a biochemistry major and study how human body works on the microscopic level.
:::

::::

After 2 semesters into my freshman year, I found a stronger interest in Physics. I liked my classes in the quantitative reasoning better than my biology classes that required a lot of memorization and less quantitative focus. I started taking more Physics and Math classes and found a really tight-knit community here in the Physics Department.

We worked on hard problems together, pulled all-nighters together in the CPL (iykyk), and went to laser tag as a class. It was a lot of fun to have a group of people doing the same thing as me and being able to understand the work that I did.
